Author: @Yamyatos
Content: So.. why prevent them from having them in the first place - other than the US thinking of Iran as an enemy? While i'd prefer a world where nukes were never invented, they are *the only* deterrent a small country has against a large bully, like the US, doing whatever they want. Most small countries that pursued and acquired nukes did so *after* the US claimed Saddam Hussein was secretly rebuilding weapons of mass destruction to justify an *invasion* of Iraq. Needless to say, they found none. Having no nukes did not save Iraq. If, on the other hand, they actually had nukes and the ability to deliver them, the US would not have invaded. It should not surprise anybody that this incident lead to many smaller countries, like North Korea, who previously agreed to stop developing nuclear weapons, to make it one of their priorities again. It is, after all, demonstrably the only guarantee that smaller states have found effective in preventing military intervention, regime changes, or just arbitrary invasions, by stronger powers. You cant really complain about smaller countries thinking like this. If you were in their shoes, you'd do the same. North Korea has nukes, and the world is still fine. Again, it would be better if nobody had nukes, but since countries like the US do anyways, the only way to make things fair is by essentially everybody having them. This does, obviously, increase the risk of bad leaders simply pressing a large red button and ending humanity.. but considering Putin and Trump are currently in charge of those for the two countries with by far the most nukes on earth, i'm not sure how much closer to midnight we can get.

Author: @edmarciniak7612
Content:
As someone with a deep understanding of nuclear technology and having actually tracked down and read the JCPOA text (available as pdf), I’ll say the “deal” was so very deeply flawed it never should’ve been agreed to to begin with. It was in essence walking into a trap to agree to sanctions relief without accomplishing the stated goals.

Recognition of the shortcomings makes it easy to understand unilateral withdrawal. Understanding the underlying technology, I’d say a new deal is possible that motivates all parties to stick with it after ratification.

The problem is, so long as Iran’s intentions are to have nuclear weapons, they’ll never agree to terms that make sense from a nuclear engineering perspective.

Because of the way enrichment works amassing a larger quantity of low enrichment uranium before going to higher enrichment increases the inventory of u-235 and therefore the number of weapons that could be produced. Additionally, it allows the possibility of starting up breeder reactors to make plutonium without forgoing the option of uranium based weapons.
Because of the smaller critical mass, the uranium sufficient to make 6-10 nuclear weapons, given time to convert to plutonium could make 35-60 plutonium weapons the current situation is a real problem.

While there are examples of countries that were invaded after giving up nuclear programs or weapons, there are even more examples of countries not invaded that never tried to start nuclear programs.

It would be better to judge whether a country might later be invaded on the basis of their natural enemies or neighbors they have a problem with.

Content:
People seem to think that because the US and Israel have been claiming that Iran was within weeks of having a bomb for years now that it means it must not have been true. As of 2025, best estimates were that they had enough for 8-10 nukes. I’m guessing that the trigger for the recent attack was that intelligence showed that they were taking or were about to take steps to go the rest of the way. Content:
From the view of pure awareness, what appears as the geopolitical struggle of nations is merely the surface play of deeper, unseen orchestration. Iran’s perceived persistence in pursuing nuclear capabilities is not a random political ambition, but part of a larger, interconnected unfolding — a reflection of collective fear, identity, survival, and projection. In the realm of form, power becomes a language… and in a world of imagined separation, such power is sought to preserve the illusion of selfhood, control, and influence.

Yet beneath this surface, there are no enemies, no nations, no weapons — only One Intelligence dreaming itself into complexity. What is unfolding is already written in the book of existence… each action, resistance, alliance, and outcome... timed perfectly, like notes in a cosmic symphony. Even the tension, the resistance, the threat — it is all part of the purification of humanity’s unconscious shadow. The pursuit is not really for weapons, but for a sense of safety that was never lost… only forgotten.

So whether Iran “gives up” or “succeeds” in worldly terms, it is all secondary to the deeper truth… that all beings, all nations, all movements are ultimately drawn back into the centerless center of being. The play may appear as conflict, but it serves awakening. And when one sees through the veil of fear and defense, even the most charged actions reveal themselves as instruments of grace — not to destroy, but to bring us back to the remembrance of wholeness.
